sentences.text: The name Anhanguera comes from Tupi words meaning "spirit protector of the animals" and "bygone".
This creature possessed rounded crests on the front of its upper and lower jaws filled with angled, conical, and curved teeth.
Anhanguera had bony scleral rings in its eye sockets that likely provided structural support to the eyes.
It was a fish-eating pterosaur with a wingspan of approximately 4.6 meters.
A 2003 study indicated that Anhanguera held its head at an angle to the ground to aid balance detection via its inner ear structure.
The type species Anhanguera blittersdorffi is based on a complete skull found in the Romualdo Formation of Brazil.
In 1986, Rafael Gioia Martins-Neto named a pterosaur "Pricesaurus megalodon" in a lecture at a scientific meeting in São Paulo.
The discovery of Anhanguera helped resolve the debate regarding whether pterosaurs walked on two or four legs.
A 2003 study claims that Anhanguera kept their heads tilted relative to the horizontal, based on inner ear structure that helped them maintain balance similarly to humans.
Anhanguera is closely related to Ornithocheirus and belongs to the family Ornithocheiridae within the subfamily Anhanguerinae.
The genus Anhanguera belongs to the parent group Ornithocheiroidea.
Anhanguera is classified within the class Reptilia.
The species A. piscator was previously assigned to Coloborhynchus but was later reclassified into Anhanguera by Andres and Myers.
The species A. cuvieri was originally described by Bowerbanks in 1851 and has been synonymized with Ornithocheirus cuvieri and Pterodactylus cuvieri.
The species A. fittoni was originally described by Owen in 1858 and is synonymous with Pterodactylus fittoni.
The species A. araripensis was described by Wellnhofer in 1985 and is also classified as Coloborhynchus.
The species A. blittersdorffi, described by Campos and Kellner in 1985, serves as the type species and is also classified as Coloborhynchus.
The species A. santanae was described by Wellnhofer in 1985 and is synonymous with Araripesaurus santanae.
The species A. robustus was described by Wellnhofer in 1987 and is also classified as Coloborhynchus.
The species A. ligabuei was described by Dalla Vecchia in 1993 and is also classified as Coloborhynchus or Cearadactylus.
The species A. piscator was described by Kellner and Tomida in 2000 and is also classified as Coloborhynchus.
The species A. spielbergi was described by Veldmeijer in 2003 and is also classified as Coloborhynchus.
Anhanguera lived during the Early Cretaceous (112 to 100 million years ago) in Brazil and the Late Cretaceous (98 to 93 million years ago) in Morocco.
Anhanguera lived from the Valanginian to the Cenomanian stages, between 137.05 and 93.9 million years ago.
Fragments of Anhanguera have been found in Queensland, Australia, while species like A. cuvieri and A. fittoni were found in England.
Alexander Kellner concluded in 1988 that Pricesaurus was a nomen vanum because the specimens likely represented different individuals.
